biography.plain_text: Randolph Hoover co-founded Xylem Tree Experts and leads XKIG, a utility infrastructure services group. Raised in a family of entrepreneurs, he studied at the University of West Alabama. His business joined Kendall Vegetation Services with private-equity backing, creating a broader platform for tree care, power-line clearance and emergency storm response.

long_biography.plain_text:
Tree-care entrepreneur Randolph Hoover wanted field crews and office staff to work from the same information. After Xylem found building its own software too costly, it adopted a mobile system that recorded inspections even without network access. Foremen could request equipment repairs from worksites, while employee qualifications were checked before crews received assignments.

Hoover also joined his brothers Benjamin and William in supporting Children's Hospital of The King's Daughters. Their donation to its children's mental health campaign honoured their brother Henry. At the hospital's Children's Pavilion, the family's story inspired sculptor Richard Stravitz to create five bronze sunflowers for a terrace garden used by children and their families.
